partners.mechanism_chain: GPI (HGNC:4520) —DISRUPTS→ Glycolysis (REACTION:R-HSA-70171); Glycolysis (REACTION:R-HSA-70171) —LEADS_TO→ Failure to thrive (HP:0001558); MMACHC (HGNC:7417) —DISRUPTS→ Cobalamin metabolism (GO:0006731); Cobalamin metabolism (GO:0006731) —DECREASES→ Cobalamin (Vitamin B12) (CHEBI:17994); Cobalamin (Vitamin B12) (CHEBI:17994) —DISRUPTS→ Homocysteine metabolism (GO:0006573); Homocysteine metabolism (GO:0006573) —INCREASES→ Homocysteine (CHEBI:17457); Homocysteine (CHEBI:17457) —LEADS_TO→ Developmental delay (HP:0001263); Homocysteine (CHEBI:17457) —LEADS_TO→ Seizures (HP:0001250). Mutations in GPI lead to a disruption in glycolysis, impacting overall cellular energy and potentially contributing to failure to thrive. Concurrently, mutations in MMACHC disrupt cobalamin metabolism, leading to impaired homocysteine metabolism, accumulation of homocysteine, and downstream neurological phenotypes like developmental delay and seizures. The shared convergence is on the downstream metabolic consequences affecting cellular function and neurological development, despite originating from distinct primary genetic defects.

partners.mechanism_chain: Glucose-6-phosphate isomerase (GPI) (HGNC:4422) —DISRUPTS→ Glucose-6-phosphate (CHEBI:17107); Glucose-6-phosphate (CHEBI:17107) —DISRUPTS→ Glycolysis (REACT:R-HSA-1435177); Glycolysis (REACT:R-HSA-1435177) —LEADS_TO→ Congenital cataracts, facial dysmorphism, and hydronephrosis (MONDO:0013275); PRKAG2 (HGNC:9185) —DISRUPTS→ Glycolysis (REACT:R-HSA-1435177); PRKAG2 (HGNC:9185) —DISRUPTS→ Pentose Phosphate Pathway (REACT:R-HSA-1900877); Glycolysis (REACT:R-HSA-1435177) —LEADS_TO→ Lethal congenital glycogen storage disease of heart (MONDO:0009867); Pentose Phosphate Pathway (REACT:R-HSA-1900877) —LEADS_TO→ Lethal congenital glycogen storage disease of heart (MONDO:0009867). Similarly, loss-of-function mutations in PRKAG2 (Disease B), a key regulator of AMP-activated protein kinase, disrupt both glycolysis and the pentose phosphate pathway. The convergence on disrupted glucose metabolism, particularly the flux through glycolysis and the pentose phosphate pathway due to upstream metabolite accumulation, links these two distinct genetic disorders.
